item.title: A 4,000-year-old jug in Turkey holds seeds of a rare flower found nowhere else on Earth
item.description: A remarkable archaeological find at Külhöyük has unveiled the oldest seed remains of 'love flower’, housed in a 4,000-year-old Hittite jug. The species, Centaurea tchihatcheffii, is currently endangered in Turkey, prompting immediate conservation initiatives. This discovery not only emphasizes the plant's ancient roots but also highlights the modern ecological challenges it faces amidst growing urban development and agricultural practices. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Skeletons Cheer Cancer Patient: Ohio display encouraged Tammy during treatment; figures stay out year-round
item.description: In Oxford, Ohio, Bill Pyle's Halloween skeleton display became a beacon of hope for Tammy during her cancer journey. After receiving a touching letter, Pyle arranged the skeletons to honor her final radiation treatment, which shifted his perspective and deepened community bonds. This display is now a year-round fixture, updated weekly, with an annual homage to Tammy, illustrating how simple decorations can uplift during tough times. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
item.description: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk. Fuente: ScienceDaily.
